findings.description: Evaluating V2 freezes caller-owned VX contract objects through evidence output.
findings.repair: Clone VX evidence before freezing output; caller-owned objects remain writable and output remains immutable.

findings.description: Malformed structures throw generic exceptions; unrecognized replay enums are admitted into a complete economic reading. Cyclic/BigInt consumed metadata also escape governed failure.
findings.repair: Validate plain input data, structural shapes, enum values and scalar declarations at the public API; reject cycles, accessors, symbols and unsupported prototypes with RegimeInputError.

findings.description: An explicit FRED sourceId is overwritten as VIX_OFFICIAL by the normalizer; row-level conflicting provenance is ignored.
findings.repair: Preserve an explicitly conflicting sourceId and mark it invalid; reject conflicting per-row source identity instead of accepting a spliced provider.

findings.description: R0 calendars and rows with future capturedAt are accepted; R2 rows with UNKNOWN replay class are admitted.
findings.repair: Enforce R0 capture bounds at row/calendar level, including R0 parents requested under R1. Reject UNKNOWN row replay in R2. Original R1 failure is retained in read-only-r1-addendum.json.

findings.description: Assembly drops row availability/status/replay and third-contract lineage, and uses lexical maximum for offset-bearing timestamps. Late or R2 parents can become eligible R0 evidence.
findings.repair: Preserve each VX contract parent availability, capture, end, status and weakest replay; take maxima by parsed instant. Apply temporal eligibility to each slot without promoting later maturities.

findings.description: Futures field is ignored and duplicate history identities silently select the first; reversing the supplied catalog changes a valid reading into INCOMPLETE.
findings.repair: Validate native Futures label against monthly identity; reject ambiguous duplicate histories; sort catalog by expiration before selecting slots.

findings.description: TICKERS, GROUPS and INITIAL_OPTIONALS are mutable exports. Mutation of TICKERS crashes subsequent evaluation.
findings.repair: Freeze ticker universe, group members and default optional profile at runtime.

findings.description: Invalid previous duration with censored=false produces an uncensored duration of two sessions.
findings.repair: Invalid or unsafe prior duration is explicitly censored; it cannot establish an uncensored run length.

findings.description: The streak loop rescans the full packet and slices the calendar once per session: O(n²) on a long same-sign history. This is a bounded-loop implementation defect, with no need for broader tuning.
findings.repair: Index eligible BTC rows once, preserving duplicate conflicts, then scan the streak once.

findings.description: One unit wiring assertion compares evaluateRegime pillars to its own evaluateCore dependency. It is self-confirming for methodology and is excluded from independent acceptance evidence. The 464 frozen golden expected values and 1930 Python expected rows are independent of TS.
Declared Next 16.3.1 and installed 16.2.7 differ before Sweeper; manifest and lock are among the 819 byte-preserved pre-Builder files.
18 existing warnings occur outside Builder files; compare exact diagnostic tuples again in final verification.
A BTC packet explicitly labeled EUR is emitted as USD millions. Native satellite series/unit declarations are not checked.
findings.repair: Enforce existing BTC series/USD millions and GLD native series/USD declarations; invalid optional data remains isolated from core.

findings.description: An adjclose array longer than timestamps is silently truncated and the malformed aligned native payload is accepted.
findings.repair: Reject unequal native adjclose/timestamp lengths with MISALIGNED_ADJCLOSE_ARRAY while retaining dated missing cells; no Close fallback.
